2854: In a canyon draw near the south shore of Lake McConaughy, with log cabins too.  Marketed as near the lake, but reviewers say the water is well off and not walkable when the lake is low. --Claude
3037: Dallas County Fair Association grounds in Adel, open to travelers outside event weeks; same-day arrivals can self-pay.  Near the North Raccoon River, but the sites are among the fair buildings. --Claude
3226: 167-acre resort in the Turkey River valley west of Clermont, between the river and 18-acre Quarry Lake, with a beach, a restaurant, mini golf, and tubes and kayaks for rent.  Many of the river and lake sites are seasonal, but nightly sites are sold, more easily midweek.  Opens about April 15. --Claude
3368: RV park at the Dodge County Fairgrounds, run by the nonprofit Dodge County Fair Association, about 4 miles east of Beaver Dam on Highway 33; it sells nights all season, not just during events.  Paved roads; Campspot lists 4 full-hookup sites on gravel, 27 with 50-amp electric and water (3 of them paved) and 20 with 30-amp electric and water.  Walk-ins can pay by cash or check at the Legion Pavilion. --Claude
3383: Nonprofit veterans' retreat run by veterans and open to everyone, with civilian stays helping to fund it; veterans get a discount code.  Also cabins and primitive tent sites. --Claude
3388: Family campground on Cranberry Lake in the Eagle River Chain of Lakes, with a heated pool, boat docks and boat rentals.  Seasonal and overnight sites are mixed, with more overnight RV sites added recently; some are tight for big rigs. --Claude
3403: Family campground at Lakewood in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, with a heated pool, a camp store, a game room and a direct link to the Oconto County ATV trails. --Claude
3416: On 52-acre Ross Lake, with more than 200 sites and cabins, many on large 45-by-60-ft grassy pads; a heated pool, mini golf, a sandy beach and a 1.5-acre swimming pond.  Seasonal campers alongside a large overnight inventory. --Claude
3453: City of Ashland park on Lake Superior's Chequamegon Bay, with a swimming beach and a pavilion; sites are sold by the night or the month. --Claude
3454: City of Ashland park on the city's western edge: 7 RV sites with water and electric and 6 primitive tent sites, with a playground, pavilions and trails along an artesian spring and Fish Creek.  Campers use the dump station at Kreher Park. --Claude
3474: Vilas County campground on 39-acre Torch Lake near Conover, with direct access to the county's ATV and UTV trails; 21 of the sites have full hookups.  Reservations for 2027 open January 5. --Claude
3478: City of Cumberland campground on an 11-acre peninsula in Beaver Dam Lake, with a swimming beach; small, and it fills fast. --Claude
3496: City of Green Lake campground on the north shore of Green Lake, with a boat launch; Hattie Sherwood Beach is across the street.  RV sites in 20-, 30- and 50-amp tiers, plus tent sites with 20-amp power; drop-ins are taken when there is room. --Claude
3499: Town of Clover campground on Lake Superior's south shore at Herbster, off Bark Point Road: RV sites with water and electric or electric only, and rustic tent sites by the lake and in the woods.  Playground; drop-ins are taken when there is room. --Claude
3505: Iron County campground, renovated in 2009: 10 paved electric sites and 4 walk-in tent sites, with an ATV and UTV wash, a pavilion, a boat ramp and ATV trail access.  Reservations open January 1. --Claude
3506: Iron County campground on Weber Lake, a 61-acre no-wake lake for trout and panfish: 9 electric sites and 2 without, with a boat launch, a swimming area and a playground.  Reservations open January 1.  The sites are reported tight and rustic, better for small rigs, so check that one fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude
3525: Iron County park on the Turtle River between Lake of the Falls and the Turtle-Flambeau Flowage, with a boat landing.  Three camping areas: the electric sites on Side 1, lakeside sites on Side 2, and showers and flush toilets on Side 3.  Open about May 1 to October 15. --Claude
3568: Iron County park on Lake Superior at Saxon, with a beach and an 81-slip marina: 26 to 31 RV sites and about 5 walk-in tent sites.  Reservations open January 1. --Claude
3581: Town of Trego campground on the Namekagon River: 25 seasonal sites, 21 nightly RV sites and 4 tent sites, with a pavilion.  A reviewer found it very clean and easy to back into. --Claude
3585: Vernon County park near Viroqua, with rustic tent, electric and full-hookup sites around a 38-acre lake, trout streams and a boat launch. --Claude
3587: Monroe County campground at Warrens on 50-acre Lake Wazeda, the county's first park (1958), with a fishing pier and a boat launch.  Sites 1-88 have electric and water and 89-94 are walk-in tent sites; 39 are reservable and 49 first-come. --Claude
3591: Village of Wausaukee park of about 40 acres on the village's northeast edge, with the Wausaukee River, a class 2 trout stream, and Evergreen Park Pond on site.  Deluxe full-hookup sites and rustic electric ones; the showers take coins. --Claude
3807: Family-owned since 1932, on Long Lake near Burr Oak, with fishing piers, a boat launch, dock slips, a swimming beach, and modern and rustic cabins; seasonal and overnight sites are mixed. --Claude
3833: Family campground on a private lake just south of Ionia, with large grassy sites and travel trailers for rent.  Reviewers say most campers are seasonal, but nightly sites are sold. --Claude
1264: Sites ring an 8-acre lake used for swimming and fishing, some on the water and some looking at it, with a boat ramp. --Claude
